topic: Is there a limit to human intelligence?
core_question: Does human cognitive performance approach a reproducible upper boundary once high-range measurement, age, domain, practice, health, and environment are modeled explicitly, and can structured education or training shift that boundary or only improve task-specific performance?

hypotheses.name: measurement_equivalence
hypotheses.prediction: high-range calibration and practice adjustment relocate or reduce apparent global plateaus

hypotheses.name: environmental_shift
hypotheses.prediction: education, health, sleep, and enrichment shift latent performance heterogeneously across domains

hypotheses.name: conditional_asymptote
hypotheses.prediction: fixed task families show individual- and domain-specific asymptotes

hypotheses.name: transfer_limitation
hypotheses.prediction: near transfer exceeds far transfer after adaptive training

hypotheses.name: network_mediation
hypotheses.prediction: brain measures partially mediate frontier differences without uniquely determining them

decision_rule: support a conditional limit only if a calibrated, practice-adjusted, domain-specific latent trajectory has a stable asymptote with uncertainty and the result survives alternate forms, active controls, and independent sites
